_comment: Per-page anchor mapping for cite_audit_apply.py. For each slug: 'anchors' lists the inline <sup data-r='ref-N'> citations on the page paired with a verified KB-canonical PMID and a short claim summary. 'keywords' filters which OTHER pool PMIDs append as the comprehensive evidence tail (ref-N+1..M). All PMIDs must exist in cite_audit/verified_pmids.json with abstracts.

anchors.claim: FIGO PALM-COEIN classification system — the 2011 framework that replaced 'dysfunctional uterine bleeding' with eight structured causes (Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy, Coagulopathy, Ovulatory, Endometrial, Iatrogenic).
2018 FIGO revision — adds intermenstrual bleeding to the formal definition and updates normal-cycle parameters (frequency 24–38 days, duration 4.5–8 days, volume 5–80 mL).
Endometrial sampling in low-risk AUB — establishes who needs a biopsy and supports Pipelle as the first-line outpatient device.
Levonorgestrel-IUS for AUB and dysmenorrhea — reduces menstrual blood loss by 71–95% versus baseline; more effective than oral progestogens and equivalent to ablation at 1 year.
Hysterectomy vs endometrial destruction vs LNG-IUS for heavy menstrual bleeding — individual-patient meta-analysis from 17 RCTs establishing the conservative-first ladder.
Nonsurgical management of heavy menstrual bleeding — head-to-head systematic review of tranexamic acid, NSAIDs, combined OCPs, and progestin regimens.
Diagnostic hysteroscopy in AUB workup — sensitivity 94% and specificity 89% for intracavitary lesions when transvaginal ultrasound is equivocal.
ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline — Diagnosis of Endometriosis. Affirms clinical diagnosis as sufficient: laparoscopy is no longer required to start treatment.
Cochrane systematic review — laparoscopic excision provides overall pain relief versus no treatment or diagnostic-only laparoscopy in endometriosis.
Vercellini et al., Fertil Steril — endometriosis and adenomyosis are associated with infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes; biology + comorbidity overview.
Hodgson et al., Fertil Steril — network meta-analysis: surgical management of endometriosis improves clinical pregnancy rates versus expectant management.
Guerriero et al., Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol — TVUS and MRI have comparable accuracy for deep infiltrating endometriosis when performed by trained operators.
Zakhari et al., Hum Reprod Update — post-operative hormonal suppression significantly reduces endometriosis and pain recurrence after excision.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 218 (summary) — Chronic Pelvic Pain: multidisciplinary framework integrating medical, surgical, physical-therapy, behavioral, and procedural layers.
Muñoz-Gómez et al., J Clin Med 2023 — 8-week manual-therapy / osteopathic protocol significantly reduced pelvic pain and improved EHP-30 quality-of-life scores in women with endometriosis.
Molins-Cubero et al., Pain Med — single sacroiliac manipulation produced immediate analgesia with measurable serotonin/catecholamine modulation in primary-dysmenorrhea pelvic pain.
Ruffini et al., Complement Ther Med — systematic review of osteopathic manipulative treatment in gynecology and obstetrics, including dysmenorrhea and pelvic pain populations.
Alboni et al., Minerva Obstet Gynecol 2024 — osteopathic visceral-fascial protocol reduced recurrent pelvic pain and dyspareunia after endometriosis surgery.
FitzGerald et al., J Urol — NIH multicenter RCT: specialized pelvic-floor myofascial physical therapy 59% response vs 26% with general therapeutic massage for urological CPP.
ESHRE Endometriosis Guideline 2022 — European multidisciplinary consensus on diagnosis, pain management, infertility, and surgery.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 218 — Chronic Pelvic Pain: multidisciplinary framework integrating medical, surgical, physical-therapy, behavioral, and procedural layers.
Cochrane systematic review — laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis-associated chronic pelvic pain improves overall pain versus no treatment or diagnostic-only laparoscopy.
FitzGerald et al., NIH multicenter RCT — specialized pelvic-floor myofascial physical therapy: 59% response rate vs 26% with general therapeutic massage for urological CPP.

Starzec-Proserpio et al., systematic review — non-pharmacological conservative therapies (manual therapy, pelvic-floor PT, exercise, mind–body interventions) reduce chronic pelvic pain intensity and improve function.
Molins-Cubero et al., double-blind RCT — a single sacroiliac manipulation produced immediate analgesia with measurable neurochemical modulation (substance P).
Del Forno et al., systematic review — pelvic-floor muscle physiotherapy improves urinary, bowel, and sexual function in women with endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain.
Cochrane review — transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) reduces pain intensity in primary dysmenorrhea and offers a non-pharmacological option for pelvic pain.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 141 — Management of Menopausal Symptoms: clinical framework for systemic + local hormone therapy and non-hormonal alternatives.
Writing Group for the Women's Health Initiative (Rossouw et al.) — RCT of estrogen + progestin in healthy postmenopausal women; the trial that reshaped MHT risk-benefit discourse.
Manson et al., JAMA — pooled 18-year follow-up of the WHI MHT trials: no significant increase in all-cause or cause-specific mortality with hormone therapy use during the trial periods.
The 2022 hormone therapy position statement of The North American Menopause Society — current consensus framework for benefit/risk by age, time-since-menopause, and route of administration.
Lederman et al., SKYLIGHT 1 RCT (Lancet 2023) — fezolinetant 45 mg significantly reduced frequency and severity of moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms versus placebo at 12 weeks.

ACOG Committee Opinion 659 — The Use of Vaginal Estrogen in Women with a History of Estrogen-Dependent Breast Cancer: low-dose vaginal estrogen reasonable when non-hormonal therapies fail, after oncology team consultation.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 228 — Management of Symptomatic Uterine Leiomyomas: medical, hormonal, interventional-radiology, and surgical pathways including hysterectomy, myomectomy, UAE, and ablation.
Baird et al., Am J Obstet Gynecol 2003 — landmark population ultrasound study: cumulative incidence of uterine leiomyoma reaches >80% in Black women and ~70% in White women by age 50.
Munro et al., FIGO PALM-COEIN classification — separates leiomyoma sub-types (FIGO 0–8) and locates fibroids within the structural causes of abnormal uterine bleeding.
Donnez & Dolmans, Hum Reprod Update 2016 — comprehensive review of fibroid management: medical therapies, focused ultrasound, UAE, radiofrequency ablation, myomectomy, and emerging targets.
Schlaff et al., ELARIS UF-1/UF-2 RCTs (NEJM 2020) — elagolix with hormonal add-back significantly reduces heavy menstrual bleeding from fibroids vs placebo over 6 months.

Goodwin et al., Obstet Gynecol 2008 (FIBROID Registry long-term outcomes) — uterine artery embolization for symptomatic leiomyomata: durable symptom relief with low re-intervention rates at 3-year follow-up.

Pritts et al., Fertil Steril 2009 — updated systematic review: submucosal fibroids reduce fertility and pregnancy rates; intramural fibroids distorting the cavity also impair outcomes; myomectomy improves implantation.
ACOG Committee Opinion 760 — Dysmenorrhea and Endometriosis in the Adolescent: framework for evaluation, NSAID + hormonal management, and indications for laparoscopy when conservative therapy fails.
Marjoribanks et al., Cochrane systematic review — NSAIDs are significantly more effective than placebo for pain relief in primary dysmenorrhea, with comparable efficacy across the class.
Wong et al., Cochrane systematic review — combined oral contraceptive pills reduce primary-dysmenorrhea pain versus placebo; effect consistent across both low- and medium-dose preparations.
Taylor et al., ELARIS EM-I/EM-II RCTs (NEJM 2017) — elagolix, an oral GnRH antagonist, significantly reduces endometriosis-associated dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain versus placebo.
Molins-Cubero et al., Pain Med — double-blind RCT: a single sacroiliac manipulation produced immediate analgesia in women with primary dysmenorrhea via measurable neurochemical modulation.
Smith et al., Cochrane systematic review — acupuncture and acupressure may reduce menstrual pain in primary dysmenorrhea, though evidence is heterogeneous and benefits modest.
Bafort et al., Cochrane systematic review — laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis-associated dysmenorrhea improves overall pain compared with no treatment or diagnostic-only laparoscopy.
Vannuccini & Petraglia, F1000Research 2019 — recent advances in understanding adenomyosis: pathophysiology, imaging criteria, and the medical + surgical management menu.
Bazot & Daraï, Fertil Steril 2018 — role of transvaginal sonography and MRI in the diagnosis of adenomyosis: TVUS as the first-line tool with MRI for inconclusive cases or surgical planning.

Bianchi et al., J Clin Med 2022 — utility of the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system for AUB and dysmenorrhea, including adenomyosis-driven heavy menstrual bleeding and quality-of-life outcomes versus hysterectomy.
Schlaff et al., ELARIS UF-1/UF-2 RCTs (NEJM 2020) — elagolix with hormonal add-back reduces heavy menstrual bleeding in fibroid/adenomyosis-overlap patients.
Younes & Tulandi, JMIG 2018 — systematic review of conservative surgery for adenomyosis: adenomyomectomy techniques, fertility outcomes, and uterine-rupture risk in subsequent pregnancy.

Harmsen et al., Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol 2022 — MUSA consensus on revised sonographic definitions of adenomyosis features (linear striations, asymmetric myometrial thickening, cystic spaces, junctional-zone irregularity).
Bafort et al., Cochrane 2020 — laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis and adenomyosis-related chronic pelvic pain improves overall pain versus no surgical treatment.

Teede et al., Fertil Steril 2023 — 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of PCOS: updates Rotterdam criteria, prioritizes AMH for diagnosis in adults, and reframes the lifelong cardiometabolic risk profile.

Rotterdam ESHRE/ASRM PCOS Consensus Workshop Group, Hum Reprod 2004 — revised 2003 consensus on diagnostic criteria (any 2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology) and long-term health risks.

Knowler et al., Diabetes Prevention Program (NEJM 2002) — landmark trial: lifestyle intervention reduced type 2 diabetes incidence by 58%, metformin by 31% in high-risk adults — foundational for PCOS metabolic management.

Legro et al., NEJM 2014 — letrozole vs clomiphene for PCOS infertility: letrozole significantly increased live births (27.5% vs 19.1%) without increased adverse outcomes — first-line ovulation induction.
Al Khalifah et al., Syst Rev 2015 — effectiveness and safety review of treatments used for PCOS (including spironolactone, OCPs, metformin for hirsutism and menstrual regulation).

Naderpoor et al., Hum Reprod Update 2015 — meta-analysis: metformin plus lifestyle is more effective than lifestyle alone for weight loss, menstrual regulation, and biochemical hyperandrogenism in PCOS.
Hoeger et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2021 — update on PCOS consequences, challenges, and guiding treatment across the lifespan: metabolic, reproductive, and psychological dimensions.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 174 — Evaluation and Management of Adnexal Masses: triage of simple vs complex, role of TVUS and CA-125, indications for surgical vs conservative management.

Van Calster et al., 2015 — practical guidance for applying the ADNEX model from the IOTA group: validated risk-stratification of adnexal masses into 5 categories (benign, borderline, stage I cancer, stage II–IV cancer, metastatic).

Levine et al., Society of Radiologists in Ultrasound consensus (Radiology 2010) — management of asymptomatic ovarian and other adnexal cysts on ultrasound: surveillance intervals by size and morphology.

ACOG Committee Opinion 716 — Role of the obstetrician-gynecologist in the early detection of epithelial ovarian cancer: screening is not recommended for average-risk women; risk-reducing salpingectomy at time of other gyn surgery is appropriate.

Kahn et al., 2023 systematic review — opportunistic salpingectomy at time of benign gynecologic surgery is associated with significant reduction in ovarian-cancer incidence; supports the salpingectomy-for-prevention strategy in average and elevated-risk women.

Liu et al., 2017 meta-analysis — laparoscopic vs open surgical approaches for adnexal masses: laparoscopy is associated with shorter hospital stay and faster recovery with equivalent oncologic outcomes for benign and borderline lesions.

Huber et al., 2021 — hormone-replacement therapy in BRCA mutation carriers and risk of ovarian, breast, and endometrial cancer: framework for hormone use after risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy in hereditary breast-ovarian cancer syndrome.

ACOG Committee Opinion 750 — Perioperative Pathways: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS): multidisciplinary bundle of pre-op carbohydrate loading, opioid-sparing anesthesia, early feeding/ambulation, multimodal analgesia.
Nelson et al., Gynecol Oncol 2016 (ERAS Society) — guidelines for postoperative care in gynecologic/oncology surgery: protocol elements that consistently reduce length of stay and complications.
Kehlet, Br J Anaesth 1997 — foundational multimodal approach to control postoperative pathophysiology and rehabilitation; the conceptual root of all subsequent ERAS pathways.
Gould et al., CHEST 2012 (ACCP Antithrombotic Therapy guideline) — prevention of VTE in nonorthopedic surgical patients including perioperative management of anticoagulant therapy.
Geerts et al., CHEST 2008 (ACCP guideline) — prevention of venous thromboembolism: risk stratification, mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis selection in surgical patients.
Massoth et al., 2021 — opioid-free anaesthesia reduces postoperative nausea, vomiting, and pain compared with opioid-based regimens; supports the multimodal-analgesia component of ERAS.

Oh et al., 2026 — perioperative risks of GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide): retained gastric contents and aspiration risk; current consensus on pre-op hold timing for daily vs weekly agents.

Winner et al., CHOICE Project (NEJM 2012) — when cost barriers are removed and women are counseled on all methods, ~75% choose LARC and the unintended-pregnancy rate drops by 50% versus typical-use methods.

U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 2024 (MMWR Recommendations and Reports) — CDC reference framework for safety of contraceptive methods by medical condition, with explicit recommendations for hypertension, migraine, postpartum, breast cancer, and other conditions.

Trussell, Contraception 2011 — contraceptive failure in the United States: typical-use vs perfect-use first-year failure rates across every method, the canonical reference for method-effectiveness counseling.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 152 — Emergency Contraception: ulipristal acetate, copper IUD, levonorgestrel options; comparative efficacy and indications including weight-based effectiveness.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 206 — Use of Hormonal Contraception in Women with Coexisting Medical Conditions: framework for cardiovascular disease, migraine, diabetes, lupus, and other comorbidities.

ACOG Committee Opinion 762 — Prepregnancy Counseling: optimal interval, folate supplementation, chronic-condition control, immunization status, lifestyle and genetic-screening considerations before conception.
Zapata et al., 2018 — updated systematic review of structured contraceptive counseling in clinical settings: interventions that improve method continuation and patient-centered decision-making.

ACOG Practice Bulletin 200 — Early Pregnancy Loss: diagnostic criteria (sonographic + β-hCG), three management pathways (expectant, medical with mifepristone+misoprostol, surgical), and Rh-D considerations.

Schreiber et al., NEJM 2018 — pretreatment with mifepristone significantly improves completion of medical management of early pregnancy loss with single-dose misoprostol (84% vs 67%) and reduces need for surgical evacuation.

ASRM Practice Committee, Fertil Steril 2020 — definitions of infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss: standardized terminology (≥2 clinically recognized losses, including biochemical and ectopic) to harmonize research and clinical practice.
ASRM Practice Committee, Fertil Steril 2026 — recurrent pregnancy loss: current committee opinion on evaluation (genetic, anatomic, endocrine, thrombophilia, immunologic) and evidence-based therapy.
ACOG Practice Bulletin 193 — Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy: diagnostic algorithm with TVUS + serial β-hCG, methotrexate criteria (single-dose vs multi-dose), and indications for surgical management.
ACOG Clinical Practice Update 2024 — Rh D Immune Globulin Administration After Early Pregnancy Loss: revised guidance on indications and dosing based on gestational age and procedure.

Herbert et al., J Affect Disord 2022 systematic review + meta-analysis — the mental health impact of perinatal loss: increased risk of depression, anxiety, PTSD, and complicated grief; framework for identifying patients needing structured support.
